summary: Relative time (“3 minuti fa”, “domani”) in a semantic <time datetime> element, formatted with Intl.RelativeTimeFormat according to the locale; the absolute date is in the title.
whenToUse: Recent activity, notifications, comments, last updated.
whenNotToUse: Deadlines, appointments or legal data: show the absolute date and time.
Dates without time (birthdays, calendar days): use Intl.DateTimeFormat on a CalendarDate.

props.name: date
props.description: Instant: Date, ISO 8601 string with offset, or epoch milliseconds.

props.name: now
props.description: Reference instant: deterministic output with no updates (tests, SSR, lists).

props.name: updateInterval
props.description: Update interval in ms when now is not set; 0 disables it.

props.name: absoluteFormat
props.description: Format of the absolute date in the title.

props.name: selectRelativeUnit(diffMs)
props.description: Pure function that picks the unit (e.g. 90 minutes → 2 hours).

inherits: HTML attributes of <time> (className, style, title, data-*); ref on the element.
accessibility: The relative text is read normally; datetime holds the ISO instant for machines and assistive technologies.
The title isn't accessible to everyone (touch, keyboard): if the exact time matters, also show it as text.
Periodic updates are not announced (no live region) to avoid disruption.
responsive: Inline text; formatStyle="short" reduces length in tight spaces.
customization: Locale from LocaleProvider; styles via className.
commonMistakes: Passing ISO strings without an offset (“2024-06-12T10:00”): they are interpreted in the browser's time zone.
Computing relative time on the server without now: the text differs between server and client (the hydration warning is suppressed, but the text changes).
limits: Months and years are approximated (30 and 365 days).
With an invalid date it renders nothing and logs a warning in development.
